summary:
Count plays per genre (ids are small, −10⁴ … 10⁴, so an array works). Then pick the k best by (count
high, id low). Sorting all genres works; a size-k heap avoids sorting everything; and because counts
are integers up to n, bucketing by count makes the whole thing linear.

question.md:
Return the `k` most-played genres, best first. Ties in play count go to the **smaller genre id**.

- **The order of the answer matters:** by count descending, then id ascending.
- **Ids can be negative** (−10⁴ … 10⁴), so shift them by 10⁴ to use them as array indices.
- **k is valid:** at least k different genres exist.
- **Size:** up to 10⁵ plays, up to 20,001 distinct genres.

**Edge cases to keep in mind**

- Ties in play count: smaller genre id first.
- `k` equals the number of genres: return all of them in order.
- Genre ids can be negative (down to −10⁴), so an array index needs an offset of 10⁴.

think.md:
**Counting is a lookup table.** Most "how many times" questions reduce to: walk the input once and keep a count per
value. The only design choice is the table:

- **A plain array** when the values are small and known in advance (26 letters, 128 characters, ids in a fixed range):
  index directly by the value.
- **A hash map (or hash set)** when values are large or unpredictable (up to 10⁹): expected O(1) per lookup.

Either way, one pass builds the counts in O(n), which is what replaces repeated scanning.
**Count, then take the best `k`.** For `[3, 1, 3, 2, 1, 3, 4, 2, 1, 5]` with `k = 3`:

The top 3 are **`[1, 3, 2]`**.

**Ways to take the best `k`:** sort all genres (O(g log g)), keep a size-`k` min-heap of the best seen so far
(O(g log k)), or, since counts are at most `n`, put genres in **buckets by count** and read from the highest
bucket down (O(n)):

approaches.title: Keep the best k in a min-heap

idea.md:
Count, then scan the genres keeping a **min-heap of size `k`** holding the best `k` so far, ordered by
`(count, −id)` so the weakest is on top. A new genre replaces the top only if it's better. At the end, sort
the heap's `k` items from best to worst.

build: Replace the weakest when a better genre appears.

lines.text: A heap entry and the ordering that matters: which of two genres is **weaker**. The weakest kept genre sits on top so it's the one we compare against and evict.

A hand-written binary min-heap (C has none). `siftUp` moves a new entry up while it's weaker than its parent; `siftDown` moves the top down, swapping with its weaker child, until the heap order holds again. Both are O(log k).
One pass over the log.
The best `k` genres seen so far, weakest on top.

notes.java: The comparator puts fewer plays first, and on ties the larger id first: that's "weakest first".
notes.cpp: `greater<>` makes a min-heap of `(plays, −id)`: the smallest pair is fewest plays, and on a tie the most negative `−id`, i.e. the largest id: the weakest.

lines.text: Every genre that was played.
Represent the genre so that "bigger means stronger".

notes.python: Tuples `(plays, −id)`: more plays is bigger, and on a tie a smaller id gives a bigger `−id`.

lines.text: Fill the heap up to k; after that, a genre only gets in by beating the weakest kept one, which it replaces.

notes.java: Simpler variant: always add, then drop the weakest if there are k + 1. Same result.
notes.cpp: Always push, then pop the weakest if there are k + 1.

lines.text: Sort the `k` winners from most to fewest plays (ties by id) and return their ids.

notes.python: Sorting the k kept tuples in reverse puts the strongest first.
notes.c: Pop by moving the last entry to the top and sifting it down; free the scratch memory.

complexity.md: **Time O(n + g log k).** **Space O(k)** for the heap.

walk.title: Keep a min-heap of the best 3 so far; its top is the weakest, and gets replaced by anything better.

limits.md: Still O(log k) per genre. Counts are bounded by `n`, so buckets avoid comparisons entirely.

approaches.title: Buckets by play count

idea.md:
Count, then drop each played genre into `bucket[count]` in increasing id order. Read buckets from the
highest count down, collecting genres until `k` are taken.

**Why the order is right.** Higher buckets come first; within a bucket, ids were appended in increasing
order, which is the tie rule.

build: Read from the highest bucket until `k` are taken.

lines.text: One pass over the log.
Each played genre goes into the bucket for its play count, in increasing id order.

notes.c: Buckets as linked lists in two arrays: `head[c]` is the first genre with count c and `next[i]` the one after `i`. Walking ids from largest to smallest and pushing to the front leaves each list in increasing id order.

lines.text: Highest count first; stop as soon as `k` genres are collected.
The top `k` genres.

notes.c: Free the scratch arrays and report the length.

complexity.md: **Time O(n + R):** counting, a pass over the id range, and the buckets. **Space O(n + R).**

steps.text: Bucket[c] lists genres played c times, smallest id first.

walk.title: Drop genres into buckets by play count (in id order), then read buckets from the top.

takeaways.md:
- **Top k by frequency:** count, then buckets (O(n)), a size-k heap (O(g log k)), or a full sort.
- Encode tie rules in the order buckets are filled or in the heap key.
- **Pitfall:** a max-heap of all genres when a size-k min-heap is enough.
